## Demonstrated inferred rule (strong confidence)
Each input contains two panels separated by a solid delimiter line/column. The output encodes the *color equalities* between corresponding cells of the two panels: output cell is 3 if the two panel cells are equal; otherwise it is the output background color. Orient panels according to delimiter: vertical delimiter => left/right halves correspond by row/column; horizontal delimiter => upper/lower panels correspond by column/row. The output panel is the corresponding overlap-sized region.

### Evidence
Demo 4 input 24x7, vertical separator col 4 of zeros. Left panel cols 1-3 contain values 5/8; right panel cols 5-7 contain 8/9. Output 24x3. Checking examples: row 2 left [5,8,5], right [9,8,8], equality at middle gives output [8,3,8]. Row 4 left [5,8,8], right [9,8,8], equal at cols 2,3 => [8,3,3]. Output background 8.
Demo 2 input has upper ten rows with 0/5 and lower ten rows with 2/5, separator row 11 all 7s. Output 10x8 background 5; each output 3 where corresponding upper and lower cells are equal. Example row1 upper [5,5,0,5,5,5,0,5], lower [2,2,5,5,5,5,2,2], equal at c4,c5,c6 => output [5,5,3,3,3,3,5,5]? Output 3x12 background 8, 3 where corresponding positions match: row2 left anomaly at c9 (8), right anomaly at c10? Output c9 marked, so investigate possible equality based on exceptions.

Right panel cols13-23 values 1 with two 6 anomalies: row3 at local col3 (global c15); row5 local col5 (global c17). Expected output likely 9x11. Left cells values {5,8}, right cells {8,9}. Equality only possible where both are 8. Output has 3 exactly where left=8 and right=8; otherwise 8. This is definitive.
For test, right panel is mostly 1, with value 6 at (r3,c3) and (r5,c5) in local coordinates. Left panel values 4/6. Thus equality occurs only at these right-side 6s when left counterpart is also 6. Inspect test left panel:

r5: [6,4,6,6,6,4,6,4,4,4,6] => local c5=6 => mark output (r5,c5)=3.

The mismatch suggests relation may be to map left pattern to right, or compare panel values differently.
